title: Pinning policy lifecycle and staff training outline
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a working outline to: (1) define the lifecycle steps for region-pinning policies (draft -> enforce -> monitor -> deprecate), (2) map operator/SE/eng roles to runbook tasks, and (3) propose a staff-training curriculum and simulation lab for safe enforcement testing.

Scope and assumptions:
- Focused on tenant-level region pins for Private and Dedicated customers.
- Excludes corporate legal contract language — legal owns contract templates referenced in linked_artifacts.
- Assumes platform supports declaration + operator-override flows and that telemetry can attach evidence bundles to incidents.
- Goal: reduce time-to-safe-enforcement and lower human error during rollouts.

High-level pin lifecycle (proposed):
1) Proposal/Request: product/sales/CS raises a region-pin request (JIRA). Draft policy created with scope, TTL, rollback criteria.
2) Validation: Eng runs simulated routing and boundary tests in staging testbed; security reviews data flows.
3) Certification: policy assigned a risk score; owner team must complete training checklist.
4) Canary enforcement: pin deployed to 1–2 non-critical tenants; synthetic traffic + real telemetry evaluated for 48–72h.
5) Gradual rollout: increase tenant cohorts, monitor cost/latency/regression signals.
6) Harden: operator runbooks updated and retention/evidence configuration baked in.
7) Deprecation/rollback: pre-defined triggers for automated rollback or manual deprecation.

Quick-reference decision matrix (short):
- If customer requires hard sovereignty (contract clause) -> Hard pin (no cross-region fallback).
- If customer allows regional preference but accepts fallback -> Soft pin (preference + audit evidence).
- If temporary legal hold -> Ephemeral pin with strict TTL and audit bundle.
- If test staging -> Simulated pin (no production enforcement).

Roles and responsibilities (operational):
- Policy owner (Product/Ent-CS): scope, business justification, acceptance criteria.
- Platform SRE/Infra: testbed simulations, rollout orchestration, telemetry hooks.
- Oncall Operators: execute canary, monitor signals, run rollback.
- Solutions Eng / SE: customer comms and runbook handover.
- Security & Legal: review for cross-border data flow, compliance signoff.

Operator playbook checklist (runbook items, quick actions):
- Pre-deploy checks (30–60 min):
  - Confirm JIRA policy id + owner contact.
  - Verify testbed simulation results attached to policy (route hit ratios, latency delta).
  - Confirm KMS key region selection matches pin.
  - Ensure monitoring dashboards have tenant-filtered views and evidence capture toggled.
- Canary deploy (t+0):
  - Announce in #pin-rollouts Slack channel with explicit cadence and contact.
  - Execute canary via orchestration (documented CLI/API) to selected tenant IDs.
  - Start synthetic traffic generator at low qps (scripting in repo).
- Observe (t+0 -> t+72h):
  - Watch latency P50/P95, model failure rate, region-assertion-misses, and evidence logs per request.
  - Capture snapshots every 15m for first 2 hours, hourly thereafter.
  - If model quality regression > pre-approved threshold or region-assertion-miss rate > 0.5% -> pause and investigate.
- Rollback criteria & actions:
  - Automatic rollback: major outage signal (latency spike, error budget burn) -> orchestration triggers rollback to prior routing config.
  - Manual rollback: triggered by operator after post-mortem discovery; follow rollback checklist and evidence collection.

Training curriculum (modular, for role-based certification):
- Module 0: Residency fundamentals (30m) — legal/geo concepts, hard vs soft pins, contract triggers.
- Module 1: Platform mechanics (1h) — how pins are represented in routing, evidence bundles, KMS implications.
- Module 2: Simulation lab (2h) — run sim harness, interpret results, simulate failovers.
- Module 3: Canary ops (1h) — execute a canary, monitor dashboards, initiate rollback.
- Module 4: Communication & customer scripts (45m) — templates for notifying customers and internal stakeholders.
- Certification: pass a tabletop + simulation scenario; operators must complete annually.

Simulation lab design (practical notes):
- Lightweight infra: use regional testbed with synthetic tenants that mirror typical traffic profiles (chat, embedding batch).
- Failure scenarios: high latency region, partial mirror loss, KMS unavailability, network egress block.
- Tools: small Python harness to create multi-tenant traffic slices, faker request headers for locale, automated evidence extraction script.
- Desired outcomes: operator can perform canary, detect anomalies, and trigger rollback within SLA window.

Staffing and shift handover best practices:
- Pre-shift checklist: operators review active pins, scheduled rollouts, and alerts backlog.
- Handover notes: short bulleted summary in oncall doc + link to last 24h snapshots.
- Warroom protocol: designate facilitator, scribe, escalation path to Eng-L2 and product owner.

Communication templates (short examples):
- Internal slack (rollout start):
  "Starting pin canary for JIRA-INF-4829 -> tenant 88, 11:00 PST. Owner: Aisha P. Escalation: Marco A. Monitor boards: /dash/region-pin/INF-4829."
- Customer notice (pre-enforcement):
  "Planned update: we will enable regional anchoring for your tenant on <date>. Expected impact: none under normal conditions; we will notify if rollback needed. Contact: solutions-eng@example.com."

Telemetry & evidence requirements (minimum):
- Per-request evidence token: region-assertion flag, KMS key id, physical-region tag, request-id.
- Aggregates: region-miss-rate, fallback-rate, latency by region, token cost delta.
- Retention: store evidence bundle for 90 days for audit by enterprise customers (configurable).

QA test cases (automated + manual):
- Routing correctness: mapping of tenant -> pinned region for 10K synthetic requests.
- Fallback behavior: ensure soft pin falls back to approved region list and logs evidence.
- Failover: simulate region outage and validate rollback triggers.
- Audit export: generate evidence package and verify all required fields present.

Open questions / unresolved items (notes to self):
- TTL enforcement: should we auto-expire ephemeral pins or require manual renewals? (ops/pm discussion).
- Evidence format: binary vs JSON bundle (tradeoffs for storage and privacy).
- Certification cadence: annual vs semi-annual? Propose annual + ad-hoc after major infra changes.

Next steps (actionable):
- Assign single owner for this lifecycle doc (Aisha to take ownership for first iteration).
- Build a 2-hour simulation lab kit in github repo (SE/Infra owners: Marco + Priya).
- Draft tabletop scenarios and acceptance criteria for certification (deadline: 2025-01-20).
- Sync with legal to confirm retention parameters (link in linked_artifacts).

Appendix: quick commands & links (work-in-progress)
- sim-harness: github.com/redwood-inference/region-pin-sim README
- dashboards: /dash/region-pin/{policy_id}
- rollouts channel: #pin-rollouts

Status: draft — this is a sketch for review. Comments welcome (particularly from SRE and Legal).

Notes to reviewers: add any missing test scenarios, propose TTL policy, and flag anything that requires platform changes (API/CLI) before we call a rollout certified.
